citations.review_text: I'd say this game is balanced but that would be a lie, especially if you use modded characters, but if it isn't some of the most fun I've had in a long time. using the characters that are base game is always fun if you want to settle some beef with a friend on equal terms, and watching the replay at the end is peak.

Beauty. I've always found there was a certain level of beauty to fighting games - the uncertain taking of steps, the consideration of each move, their timing and hitboxes clashing and overlapping like a dance.

Nevertheless, seldom have I experienced that beauty first-hand during play, my contact with these sort of games mostly dominated by the constant panicking over motion inputs and attack strings. I knew the words to say, but my brain couldn't quite figure out how to translate them to buttons.

Enter YOMI Hustle - a game where these sort of issues fizzle away and give way to pure, unadulterated expression. It's a dance born of purpose, of adversity, and also, of connection. To defeat an enemy you must know them, read their minds and paint their brains. And when you finish the dance, no matter who the winner is, the result is always that beautiful painting at the end - the match replay.

I can't stop watching the match replays. They're so fun to watch. They remind me of kung fu movies and flash animations. They're also something that I made. That we made. Together, against each other.

This game is absurdly fun, and while it's much easier to learn than most fighting games due to its lack of execution requirements, it still has extremely deep skill expression in its mixups, neutral, mindgames, and combo routes. It forces you to stop and think about every move you make while also forcing you to make a choice in a limited period of time, which often gives you enough rope to hang yourself by overthinking things. But not thinking about it is also a huge risk due to the sheer amount of moves every character has available to them, meaning that if you don't consider all the options you and your opponent have, you're liable to miss something important and end up eating damage or dropping a combo because of it.

The built-in modding support is also top-notch, and allows for so much customization that I don't know if there even is a limit to what you can do with it. There's a mod on the workshop that replaces the game with Doom. You can run Doom on YOMI Hustle.

All of that, just for $5.
One of the best fighting games on the market, especially since it has workshop support.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features extensive mod support with a large catalog of workshop characters that add significant longevity and variety.

citations.review_text:
This has to be one of the most brilliant fighting games I've ever played, and the possibilities and potential becomes endless with the workshop support it has.  I have seen, and done things in this game that I cannot imagine being replicated in any other game out there.  

The fighting moves characters are given and presented with can range from elegant simplicity to downright god destroying moves to confusing yourself and your opponent with diverse complexity- all with unreactable nuance (unreactable as in when you watch the replay afterwards, not in gameplay.)  

The thrill that the fights give in this game is enough alone to just always be having fun and I can't even be mad when im getting my ass beat either because the techniques and moves that you get to see from modded characters are largely unexpected and cool as f*ck.  (like Miko, Illuko, Adans, Chara, etc. on the workshop)

This game visually looks complex but it might as well be misleading because- trust me it's an incredibly easy game to play and pick up, so long as you understand that the buttons on the bottom of the screen on the left half is for P1 and buttons on the right half is for P2, I believe no matter your skill level or familiarity with fighting games you will always have a good time on this game.

And if you have any know-how on programming and/or making art and sprites, you can make characters from what I've heard to be fairly easily through the Godot engine and Modded characters can be just about anything you want them to be and do almost anything you want them to do so long as you figure that out. 

Please pick up this game and KEEP ON HUSTLING.
